To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription of DNA by RNA polymerase is inhibited by actinomycin by a mechanism which requires that the actinomycin be bound to a premelt region of DNA.
actinomycin D binds to the premelted DNA in a transcription complex and thereby interferes with the elongation step of RNA synthesis.

(i) actinomycin does not bind to DNA in solution but only in a premelted conformation; (ii) the premelted conformance is present in the transcriptional complex and is stabilized by the RNA-DNA hybrid; (iii) actinomycins binds to this conformation, immobilizing it and preventing RNA elongation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the transcription of DNA to RNA in the cell.
the mechanism of action of actinomycin D, an antibiotic that inhibits the transcription of DNA into RNA.
the structure and function of nucleic acids and their interactions with other molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
actinomycin does not inhibit transcription, it inhibits the elongation of nascent chains.
actinomycin is an inhibitor of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
actinomycin inhibits transcription of DNA by preventing the elongation of RNA chains by binding to premelted DNA within the transcriptional complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that transcription is a highly ordered process, with the RNA chain elongation being a rate-limiting step.
the actinomycin model is a good one, and that we are now beginning to understand some of the implications of the model.
the actinomycin binding site is not the transcriptional complex but is the premelted DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
actinomycin is a very effective transcription inhibitor.
the transcriptional complex is not a static structure, but rather a dynamic one that is constantly undergoing changes in its conformation.
actinomycin is not an inhibitor of transcription initiation, but an inhibitor of transcription elongation.
